summary: npm package ships obfuscated PowerShell reflective loader as its sole content
details: The tarball contains only package.json plus two identical copies of a PowerShell script (`client` and `json.txt`). The script assembles a large base64 string from ~150 small chunk variables, Base64-decodes it, XORs each byte with 89, and executes the resulting bytes via `[Scriptblock]::Create(...)` constructed reflectively from character-code-built type and method names. Supporting behaviors include hiding the console window, moving the window off-screen, and sleeping a randomized delay before execution, plus hundreds of dead-code arithmetic/string assignments interleaved around the payload to defeat static scanners. The npm manifest declares `main: index.js` but no `index.js` is present in the tarball, so the package has no legitimate JavaScript library function; its sole shipped content is the obfuscated PowerShell loader. The reflective `Scriptblock::Create` of an XOR+base64 decoded blob, combined with window-hiding and junk-code padding, is a standard malware loader shape with no legitimate use.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
